Tom — thanks, happy to help. Quick answers and next steps: 

1) SSO proof we accept
- Preferred: SAML metadata XML (file) or a signed metadata endpoint (URL).
- Acceptable but slower: screenshot showing metadata export plus a DNS TXT proving domain ownership (we use this to validate the entity).
- Not acceptable: only a user-level screenshot of the IdP without export or DNS proof.

2) Delegated uploads
- Yes, we can provision a Vendr uploader account scoped to Greenridge. Please give us a single delegated user email (security_ops@greenridgehealth.com is fine). We will send an invite with a temporary password and a short uploader playbook.

3) Filenaming and evidence guidance
- Use prefix GH-SOC2-<control>-YYMMDD (e.g., GH-SOC2-CC6.1-261002.pdf).
- Attach a one-line metadata note in the upload comments with the control mapping.

I've attached a light SIG playbook and a short SSO checklist. Mina (security operations) and Karthik (portal integrator) are copied to help with the upload and any policy questions. Can you confirm: will you provide a saml-metadata.xml or do you prefer the DNS ownership route?

Best,

Camila / Karthik — short answers from security ops: 

- Vendr ingestion: we prefer the raw XML (saml-metadata.xml). Our parser will accept an HTTPS-hosted metadata URL, but the URL must serve a stable, signed metadata file (no redirects to a login page). If they give a URL we will fetch and archive the XML.
- Minimum uploader permission: "evidence_uploader" role (upload/create comments, but no deletion or account management). We will create an audit-only identity for the uploader.
- If they cannot export XML, DNS TXT + screenshot is an acceptable temporary proof but we need a remediation ticket to collect the XML within 30 days.

I'll prepare a short checklist and the uploader invite text. Camila, I recommend we ask for: saml-metadata.xml attachment, delegated uploader email, and the target time window for evidence handoff. I'm attaching the SSO checklist we use internally.

Mina Haddad
Security Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
